# Plan: article-like-button

<!-- Generated by /plan (planner subagent). Human reviews before /implement starts. -->

## Open questions

- None.

## Technical approach

This feature stays entirely inside the article-view layer and uses in-memory UI state only. The work should follow the existing component and testing conventions, especially the guidance in `component-conventions` and `testing-rtl-msw`, while keeping the implementation isolated from backend persistence or authentication concerns.

The flow is straightforward:

- Render a lightweight like control next to the article content when the article is loaded and likes are supported.
- Default the count to `0` whenever the value has not been initialized, so the UI never renders an empty or invalid number.
- Add a click handler that increments the current local value by one and re-renders immediately.
- Guard the control in the article layout so unsupported pages either hide or disable it without disturbing the rest of the article structure.

This is intentionally a front-end-only task; there is no requirement for a user identity, undo flow, analytics, or persistence beyond the current in-memory article state.

## Files to touch

- `src/components/ArticleLikeButton.tsx` — new like-button and count UI.
- `src/features/article/ArticleView.tsx` — mount the control in the article layout and respect the likes-supported condition.
- `src/state/articleLikes.ts` or equivalent local article-state module — hold the in-memory counter value for the current article instance.
- `tests/unit/article-like-button.test.tsx` — verify the default value, increment behavior, and unsupported-page fallback.

## Risks

- The article page may already have a feature-flag or conditional rendering path for optional UI; this must be respected to avoid adding the control where likes are not supported.
- In-memory state should remain local to the article view and must not be mistaken for persisted data or user identity.
- There is no backend contract in scope, so the implementation should test only the visible UI behavior expected by the spec.
